MAINTENANCE AND ENHANCEMENT OF LONG TERM PRODUCTIVITY
Regulation of nonpassenger automobile fuel economy results in a reduction of fuel consumed. Also, less cast iron and steel will be required in the use of smaller engines and other weight reduction actions. This produces a secondary effect on the amount of energy required to manufacture automobiles. However, replacement of heavier metalic components will increase the use of plastics and aluminum. The net effect is a long term saving of oil.
OTHER INTERESTS AND CONSIDERATIONS OF FEDERAL POLICY
THAT ARE THOUGHT TO OFFSET THE ADVERSE ENVIRONMENTAL
EFFECTS OF THE ACTION
The depletable nature and uncertain availability of most of the energy upon which the Nation relies for its economic and social well being necessitates a national program for conserving energy. The gasoline shortages of the winter of 1973-1974 and the inflationary effect of rising fuel costs on almost all goods and services emphasize the need for conserving petroleum.
